questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kyrgyzstan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kyrgyzstan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kyrgyzstan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kyrgyzstan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kyrgyzstan article.

questions.proof: It has borders with China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It was a socialist republic of the Soviet Union, but became independent in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kyrgyzstan article.

questions.proof: It was a socialist republic of the Soviet Union, but became independent in 1991.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Its trade partners are _____, Russia, China, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Russia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Kyrgyzstan article, under the heading “Economy”.

questions.proof: Its trade partners are Germany, Russia, China, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan.
